must_remember: The time period of a compound pendulum is given by $T = 2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{I}{m g h}}$ for small oscillations ($\theta < 4^\circ$).
The equivalent length of a simple pendulum is $L_{eq} = \frac{I}{m h} = h + \frac{k_G^2}{h}$.
The centers of suspension and oscillation are mutually interchangeable without altering the time period.
The time period is minimum when the distance of the pivot from the center of mass equals the radius of gyration ($h = k_G$).
The mass $m$ of the rigid body cancels out in the expression for the time period for uniform bodies.

glossary.meaning: Any rigid body suspended about a horizontal axis that is free to oscillate in a vertical plane under gravity.
The root-mean-square distance of the mass particles of the body from the axis passing through the center of mass.
A point situated at a distance $L_{eq}$ from the axis of suspension along the line passing through the center of mass.
The length of an equivalent simple pendulum whose time period matches that of the compound pendulum.
